licence.title: Physician Assistant license
licence.renewalDeadline: December 31 of even-numbered years (current period January 1, 2025 to December 31, 2026)

ce.categoryRules: Renewal requires meeting NCCPA continuing medical education and recertification requirements (including the NCCPA recertification exam) and holding current NCCPA certification; the state sets no separate hour total.

topicMandates.topic: Pain management and opioid use and addiction
topicMandates.appliesTo: Not yet verified for PA renewal. Confirmed for PAs at initial licensure only when holding or applying for DEA (12 AAC 40.400(b)(7)). AS 08.64.312(b) requires it of licensees of medicine, osteopathy and podiatry; SB 89 (effective 2026-09-16) adds PAs only to the exemption clause (c).

ce.controlledSubstanceCe: 2 hours pain management and opioid use and addiction at initial licensure for DEA holders (12 AAC 40.400(b)(7)); whether it recurs at each PA renewal is not yet verified.

practice.agreementFilingAndRenewal: Under regulations 12 AAC 40.410 a collaborative plan must be filed with the division within 14 days of its effective date or of any change; renewal attests to an active plan. SB 89 (Chapter 21 SLA 26, effective 2026-09-16) replaces this with a written collaborative agreement: the PA attests at licensure and renewal and provides the agreement to the board on request; PAs at physician directed facilities, licensed health care facilities, federal or tribal facilities, FQHCs, rural health clinics, military and veterans facilities, or with board authorization may practice without one.
practice.notes: Board regulations had not yet been revised to match SB 89 when loaded; the 2025 to 2026 renewal form still asks for collaborative plan verification.

prescribing.ceForPrescribers: 2 hours pain management and opioid use and addiction; PDMP registration within 30 days of licensure or DEA registration. Controlled substance prescribing needs a DEA number on file and authorization in the collaborative plan (pre SB 89 regulations).

rn.renewalDeadline: November 30 of even-numbered years (current period ends November 30, 2026)
rn.ceNote: Continuing competency: two of three per cycle: 30 contact hours of CE, 30 hours of uncompensated professional activities, or 320 hours of nursing employment (or an alternative such as a refresher course). Alternatives: a board-approved refresher course or passing NCLEX after the last renewal (12 AAC 44.640). A nurse first licensed in the second year of the period first complies before the second renewal. Of the 30 CE hours, at least 20 must be from ANCC, ACCME, ACPE, NP-certifying-body or board-approved sponsors.

aprn.title: APRN (Advanced Practice Registered Nurse)
aprn.separateLicenceOrCertificate: Separate APRN license; prescriptive authority and controlled substance authority are separate board authorizations renewed with it
aprn.ceNote: Renewal requires current national certification in each role and population focus. 12 AAC 44.400(a)(4) requires 60 contact hours every two years only where the certifying body has no CE requirement.
aprn.pharmacologyNote: 15 contact hours of advanced pharmacology within 2 years before applying for prescriptive authority (one-time at application). Renewal of prescriptive authority requires national certification showing completion of the certifying body's CE.

topicMandates.topic: Pain management and opioid use and addiction

prescribing.pharmacologyCeForPrescribers: 15 contact hours within 2 years before the prescriptive authority application (one-time); no separate state pharmacology hours at renewal.
prescribing.controlledSubstanceCe: 2 hours pain management and opioid use and addiction each licensing cycle for DEA holders with controlled substance authority.
prescribing.stateCsNote: No separate state controlled substance registration; Schedule II to V authority is a Board of Nursing authorization (12 AAC 44.445) plus DEA and PDMP registration.

practice.agreementFilingAndRenewal: None. The collaborative relationship rule (12 AAC 44.410) was repealed in 1984; no transition to practice hours found in 12 AAC 44.

unverified: PA: whether the 2 hour pain management and opioid CE (AS 08.64.312(b)) applies at each PA renewal. Statute subsection (a) names licensees of medicine, osteopathy and podiatry; SB 89 adds PAs only to the exemption clause; 12 AAC 40.470 and the renewal form do not require it. Show as not yet verified with the board link.

PA: SB 89 (Chapter 21 SLA 26, effective 2026-09-16) replaces the filed collaborative plan with a written agreement plus attestation and facility exemptions; 12 AAC 40.410's 14 day filing rule was still in the regulations when loaded and conflicts with the new statute. Treat the statute as controlling.
Board web pages on commerce.alaska.gov are behind a bot check; board PDFs (renewal forms) on the same host loaded and were used.
NP: Nurse Licensure Compact non-membership rests on HB 131 and SB 124 (34th Legislature) remaining in committee (status date 2025-03-10); a negative cannot be quoted from statute.

No other topic mandates (implicit bias, human trafficking, child abuse, ethics, HIV, end of life, Alzheimer, suicide, infection control, cultural competency, domestic violence) were found in 12 AAC 40, 12 AAC 44 or the renewal forms as loaded; the federal one-time 8 hour MATE training is federal.

corrections: PA: 2 hour pain management/opioid CE every cycle downgraded to verified:false. AS 08.64.312(a) covers licensees of medicine, osteopathy and podiatry; SB 89 sec. 9 changes only the exemption subsection (c); neither 12 AAC 40.470 nor the PA renewal form requires it. The researcher had marked it verified:true while listing the doubt in 'unverified'.
PA: added SB 89 sec. 3 (new AS 08.64.206) requiring current NCCPA certification at licensure, and the renewal form's NCCPA attestation.
NP: 'full' practice now also rests on AS 08.68.850(1) (no physician element); noted that the 44.475(f)(1) quote is a reinstatement definition.
NP: APRN renewal deadline quote replaced; the researcher quoted the next period's heading (2026-12-01 to 2028-11-30) rather than the lapse sentence.
